paragraphs: Jephthah gets driven out by his brothers, and later, when the Ammonites show up, the elders of Gilead come to get him (Judges 11:2, 11:5). He could have slammed the door. Instead he asks his question, "Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?" (Judges 11:7), makes his terms clear, and then he goes (Judges 11:11). I think that's a man who got hurt and still showed up, friend.

Now look at how he handles the king of the Ammonites. He doesn't just charge in. He sends messengers and asks, "What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?" (Judges 11:12). Then he lays out what the LORD did for Israel: the LORD delivered Sihon and his people into Israel's hand (Judges 11:21). His whole argument rests on that. The land is a gift from the LORD, the God of Israel (Judges 11:23).

So here's the big idea for you, baker. What God gives, He gives, and that's something solid to stand on when someone comes to argue. Jephthah knew his history, and he named it out loud with the LORD as Judge (Judges 11:27). Get to know the Word like that, and you'll know what you stand on when the pressure shows up. The king of the Ammonites paid no heed (Judges 11:28), and the story isn't over.
